THE DANIEL R. ABERNATHY SUPPLEMENTAL NEEDS TRUST

A first-party trust established under 42 U.S.C. Section 1396p(d)(4)(A)

THIS TRUST AGREEMENT is made on May 18, 2026 between Daniel R. Abernathy, an individual residing in Multnomah County, Oregon (the "Beneficiary"), acting through Susan Abernathy, his mother, as Grantor, and Willamette Fiduciary Services, LLC, an Oregon limited liability company (the "Trustee").

RECITALS

A. The Beneficiary is 27 years old, was born on February 3, 1999, and has a disability as defined in Section 1614(a)(3) of the Social Security Act, 42 U.S.C. Section 1382c(a)(3).

B. The Beneficiary is the plaintiff in a personal-injury action settled for $1,400,000 net of fees and costs, and those funds are the Beneficiary's own assets.

C. The Grantor establishes this Trust for the sole benefit of the Beneficiary under 42 U.S.C. Section 1396p(d)(4)(A) so that the settlement proceeds do not disqualify the Beneficiary from Supplemental Security Income or Oregon Medicaid.

ARTICLE I. ESTABLISHMENT AND FUNDING

1.1 Establishment. The Grantor transfers to the Trustee the property described on Schedule A, to be held, administered, and distributed under this Trust Agreement. The Trust is named the Daniel R. Abernathy Supplemental Needs Trust.

1.2 Sole Benefit. This Trust is established and shall be administered for the sole benefit of the Beneficiary during the Beneficiary's lifetime.

1.3 Irrevocability. This Trust is irrevocable. Neither the Grantor, the Beneficiary, nor any other person may revoke, amend, or terminate it except as Article VI permits.

ARTICLE II. DISTRIBUTIONS

2.1 Supplemental, Not Substitute. The Trustee shall distribute income and principal only for the supplemental care of the Beneficiary — goods and services that public benefits do not provide. The Trustee shall not make any distribution that would supplant, reduce, or replace any benefit the Beneficiary receives or is eligible to receive from any federal, state, or local program, including Supplemental Security Income and Medicaid.

2.2 Sole and Absolute Discretion. All distributions are in the Trustee's sole and absolute discretion. The Beneficiary has no right to compel a distribution, no power to direct the Trustee, and no vested interest in income or principal.

2.3 Examples of Permissible Distributions. Permissible supplemental distributions include, without limitation: dental, vision, and other uncovered medical care; therapies and equipment public benefits do not cover; a personal attendant; education and training; a computer, telephone, and internet service; recreation, travel, and companionship; and the purchase and maintenance of a vehicle for the Beneficiary's use.

2.4 No Cash to the Beneficiary. The Trustee shall not distribute cash directly to the Beneficiary, and shall pay providers and vendors directly, so that a distribution is not treated as income under the Social Security Administration's rules.

2.5 In-Kind Support and Maintenance. The Trustee may pay for food or shelter when the Trustee determines the benefit to the Beneficiary outweighs any reduction in Supplemental Security Income under the in-kind support and maintenance rules.

ARTICLE III. SPENDTHRIFT

3.1 Spendthrift Provision. No interest of the Beneficiary in income or principal is subject to voluntary or involuntary alienation, anticipation, assignment, pledge, sale, or transfer, and no such interest is subject to the claims of any creditor of the Beneficiary, except as 42 U.S.C. Section 1396p(d)(4)(A) requires on the Beneficiary's death.

ARTICLE IV. THE TRUSTEE

4.1 Powers. The Trustee has all powers conferred by the Oregon Uniform Trust Code, ORS Chapter 130, and by this Trust Agreement, including the power to invest, to sell, to employ agents and advisors, and to compromise claims.

4.2 Standard of Care. The Trustee shall administer the Trust in good faith, in accordance with its terms and purposes, and in the interests of the Beneficiary, and shall invest under the Oregon Uniform Prudent Investor Act.

4.3 Accounting. The Trustee shall provide an annual accounting to the Beneficiary, to the Beneficiary's legal representative, and to the Oregon Health Authority on its request, and shall retain records for six years.

4.4 Compensation. The Trustee is entitled to reasonable compensation in accordance with its published fee schedule in effect from time to time, and to reimbursement of expenses properly incurred.

4.5 Resignation and Successor. The Trustee may resign on sixty (60) days' written notice to the Beneficiary and the Beneficiary's legal representative. Susan Abernathy may appoint a successor corporate trustee; if she is unable or unwilling to do so, a court of competent jurisdiction shall appoint one. No individual may serve as trustee.

ARTICLE V. MEDICAID PAYBACK

5.1 Reimbursement on Death. On the death of the Beneficiary, the Trustee shall pay from the remaining trust property, before any other distribution and before any payment of debts of the Beneficiary's estate other than as this Article permits, an amount equal to the total medical assistance paid on behalf of the Beneficiary by any state Medicaid program, to each such state, as required by 42 U.S.C. Section 1396p(d)(4)(A).

5.2 Permitted Prior Payments. Before the reimbursement required by Section 5.1, the Trustee may pay only: taxes due from the Trust to a state or to the United States by reason of the Beneficiary's death; and reasonable fees for the administration of the Trust, such as trustee fees and accounting costs, related to the winding up of the Trust.

5.3 Not Payable. The Trustee shall not pay from the Trust, before the Medicaid reimbursement required by Section 5.1, any of the following: funeral or burial expenses; debts owed to third parties; or any distribution to a residual beneficiary.

5.4 Notice. The Trustee shall notify the Oregon Health Authority, and the Medicaid agency of any other state that has provided medical assistance to the Beneficiary, within thirty (30) days after the Trustee learns of the Beneficiary's death.

ARTICLE VI. TERMINATION AND REMAINDER

6.1 Termination. This Trust terminates on the death of the Beneficiary, or earlier if the Trustee determines that the trust property is insufficient to justify the cost of administration and that termination is in the Beneficiary's interest, in which case the Trustee shall distribute the remaining property for the Beneficiary's sole benefit consistent with Article II.

6.2 Remainder. After the reimbursement required by Article V, the Trustee shall distribute the remaining property to Susan Abernathy if she survives the Beneficiary, and otherwise to the Beneficiary's then-living descendants, per stirpes, and if none, to the Oregon Community Foundation.

ARTICLE VII. GENERAL

7.1 Governing Law. This Trust is governed by the laws of the State of Oregon, and shall be construed and administered to comply with 42 U.S.C. Section 1396p(d)(4)(A) and the rules of the Social Security Administration governing Supplemental Security Income.

7.2 Construction to Preserve Eligibility. If any provision of this Trust would disqualify the Beneficiary from any public benefit, that provision is void to the extent of the disqualification, and this Trust shall be construed to preserve the Beneficiary's eligibility.

7.3 Amendment. The Trustee may amend this Trust only to comply with a change in federal or state law affecting the Beneficiary's eligibility for public benefits, and shall give the Oregon Health Authority thirty (30) days' notice before doing so.

7.4 Situs. The situs of the Trust is Oregon. The Trustee may change the situs to another jurisdiction if doing so is in the Beneficiary's interest and does not affect eligibility.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Trust Agreement on the date first written above.
